@staticmethod
def wemmert_gancarski_index(
    X: torch.Tensor, labels: torch.Tensor, n_components: Optional[int] = None,
    metric: str = 'euclidean', noise_label: Optional[int] = None,
    VI: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
) -> float:
    r"""
    Wemmert-Gancarski index: higher is better.

    $$ R(x) = \frac{d(x, c_{\text{own}})}{\min_{j \neq \text{own}} d(x, c_j)},
       \qquad J_k = \max\left(0, 1 - \overline{R(x)}_{x \in C_k}\right),
       \qquad \text{WG} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_k n_k J_k $$

    Ranked among the best-performing internal indexes in the Simpson,
    Campello & Stojanovski (2025) benchmark.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X : torch.Tensor
        Data, shape (n_samples, n_features). `metric='precomputed'` is
        not supported (no coordinate space to average a centroid in).
    labels : torch.Tensor
        Cluster labels. Need not be contiguous or 0-indexed when
        `n_components` is left `None`.
    n_components : int, optional
        Number of clusters. If `None` (default), inferred from the
        distinct values in `labels`.
    metric : str, optional
        One of 'euclidean', 'manhattan', 'cosine', 'mahalanobis'
        (requires `VI`). (default: 'euclidean')
    noise_label : int, optional
        Label value marking noise points; dropped before computing the
        index, result scaled by `(n - n_noise) / n`. (default: None)
    VI : torch.Tensor, optional
        `(d, d)` precision matrix for `metric='mahalanobis'`.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Wemmert-Gancarski index (higher is better).
    """
    ClusteringMetrics._require_coordinate_metric(metric, 'wemmert_gancarski_index')
    original_labels = labels
    dense_labels, n_clusters, keep_mask = ClusteringMetrics._resolve_labels(
        labels, n_components, noise_label
    )
    X_eff = X[keep_mask]
    dense_labels = dense_labels.to(X_eff.device)
    n = X_eff.shape[0]

    centroids = ClusteringMetrics._cluster_centroids(X_eff, dense_labels, n_clusters)
    D = ClusteringMetrics._pairwise_distances(X_eff, centroids, metric, VI)  # (n, K)
    idx = torch.arange(n, device=X_eff.device)
    own_dist = D[idx, dense_labels]
    D_others = D.clone()
    D_others[idx, dense_labels] = float('inf')
    min_other = D_others.min(dim=1).values

    R = own_dist / min_other.clamp_min(1e-300)
    counts = torch.bincount(dense_labels, minlength=n_clusters).to(X_eff.dtype)
    sum_R = torch.zeros(n_clusters, dtype=X_eff.dtype, device=X_eff.device)
    sum_R.scatter_add_(0, dense_labels, R)
    mean_R = sum_R / counts.clamp_min(1)
    J = torch.clamp(1.0 - mean_R, min=0.0)

    value = ((counts * J).sum() / n).item()
    return ClusteringMetrics._apply_noise_scaling(value, original_labels, noise_label, maximize=True)

@staticmethod
def dunn_index(
    X: torch.Tensor, labels: torch.Tensor, n_components: Optional[int] = None,
    metric: str = 'euclidean', noise_label: Optional[int] = None,
    chunk_size: int = 4096, VI: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
) -> float:
    r"""
    Compute the Dunn index:

    $$ D = \frac{\min_{i \neq j} d(C_i, C_j)}{\max_k \mathrm{diam}(C_k)} $$

    Where:
    - $d(C_i, C_j)$ is the minimum distance between any points in clusters i, j.
    - $\mathrm{diam}(C_k)$ is the maximum distance between any points in cluster k.

    Higher Dunn index indicates better cluster separation.

    .. note::
       Ranked 25th of 26 indexes on partition ranking in the Simpson,
       Campello & Stojanovski (2025) clustering-validity benchmark --
       kept here for completeness/familiarity, not as a recommended
       choice. Prefer `wb_index`, `wemmert_gancarski_index`, or `dbcv`,
       which ranked at the top of that benchmark.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X : torch.Tensor
        Data, shape (n_samples, n_features), or an (n, n) precomputed
        distance matrix when `metric='precomputed'`.
    labels : torch.Tensor
        Cluster labels. Need not be contiguous or 0-indexed when
        `n_components` is left `None`.
    n_components : int, optional
        Number of clusters. If `None` (default), inferred from the
        distinct values in `labels`.
    metric : str, optional
        One of 'euclidean', 'manhattan', 'cosine', 'mahalanobis'
        (requires `VI`), or 'precomputed'. (default: 'euclidean')
    noise_label : int, optional
        Label value marking noise points; dropped before computing the
        index, result scaled by `(n - n_noise) / n`. (default: None)
    chunk_size : int, optional
        Row-chunk size for the pairwise-distance computation. (default: 4096)
    VI : torch.Tensor, optional
        `(d, d)` precision matrix for `metric='mahalanobis'`.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Dunn index (higher is better).
    """
    original_labels = labels
    dense_labels, n_clusters, keep_mask = ClusteringMetrics._resolve_labels(
        labels, n_components, noise_label
    )
    X_eff = X[keep_mask][:, keep_mask] if metric == 'precomputed' else X[keep_mask]
    dense_labels = dense_labels.to(X_eff.device)

    max_intra = 0.0
    min_inter = float('inf')
    start = 0
    for D_chunk in ClusteringMetrics._pairwise_chunked(X_eff, metric, chunk_size, VI):
        end = start + D_chunk.shape[0]
        row_labels = dense_labels[start:end]
        same = row_labels.unsqueeze(1) == dense_labels.unsqueeze(0)
        diff = ~same
        if same.any():
            max_intra = max(max_intra, D_chunk[same].max().item())
        if diff.any():
            min_inter = min(min_inter, D_chunk[diff].min().item())
        start = end

    value = (min_inter / max_intra) if max_intra > 0 else 0.0
    return ClusteringMetrics._apply_noise_scaling(value, original_labels, noise_label, maximize=True)

docs.title: dbcv(X, labels, metric='euclidean', noise_label=-1, VI=None) staticmethod
docs.text:
Density-Based Clustering Validation (Moulavi, Jaskowiak, Campello, Zimek & Sander, 2014). Higher is better, range [-1, 1].

For each cluster :math:C, the all-points core distance of a point :math:x \in C (not the k-NN core distance HDBSCAN itself uses) is

.. math:: a_{\text{coredist}}(x) = \left( \frac{1}{|C| - 1} \sum_{y \in C, y \neq x} d(x, y)^{-d_{\text{features}}} \right)^{-1 / d_{\text{features}}}

and the mutual-reachability distance within :math:C is :math:d_{\text{mreach}}(x, y) = \max(a_{\text{coredist}}(x), a_{\text{coredist}}(y), d(x, y)). A minimum spanning tree is built over each cluster's own mutual-reachability graph (reusing tgmm.hdbscan.prim_mst, the same Prim's-algorithm implementation HDBSCAN itself uses). Density Sparseness of a Cluster (DSC) is the maximum edge weight in that MST; Density Separation between a Pair of Clusters (DSPC) is the minimum mutual-reachability distance between an internal node (MST degree >= 2 -- excludes boundary/leaf points) of one cluster's MST and an internal node of the other's.

.. note:: For a tree with >= 3 nodes, every edge has at least one endpoint of degree >= 2 (an edge between two degree-1 nodes would disconnect the rest of the tree) -- so restricting DSC to "edges incident to an internal node" is equivalent to no restriction at all for any cluster with >= 3 points, which is why DSC below is simply the MST's maximum edge weight. The internal/leaf distinction is only load-bearing for DSPC, which compares nodes across two different clusters.

.. math:: V(C_i) = \frac{\min_j \text{DSPC}{ij} - \text{DSC}_i} {\max(\min_j \text{DSPC}, \qquad \text{DBCV} = \sum_i \frac{n_i}{n} V(C_i)}, \text{DSC}_i)

with n counting noise points in the denominator (not the numerator) -- this is dbcv's noise handling, which is why it does not go through _apply_noise_scaling the way the other internal indexes do.

Clusters with fewer than 2 points contribute 0 (the all-points core distance needs at least one other point in the cluster to average over); a cluster whose MST has no internal nodes at all (every node is a leaf -- only possible for 2-point clusters) falls back to treating every node as internal for DSPC purposes, the standard practical fallback.

@staticmethod
def dbcv(
    X: torch.Tensor, labels: torch.Tensor, metric: str = 'euclidean',
    noise_label: Optional[int] = -1, VI: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
) -> float:
    r"""
    Density-Based Clustering Validation (Moulavi, Jaskowiak, Campello,
    Zimek & Sander, 2014). Higher is better, range `[-1, 1]`.

    For each cluster :math:`C`, the **all-points core distance** of a
    point :math:`x \in C` (not the k-NN core distance HDBSCAN itself
    uses) is

    .. math::
        a_{\text{coredist}}(x) = \left( \frac{1}{|C| - 1}
            \sum_{y \in C, y \neq x} d(x, y)^{-d_{\text{features}}}
        \right)^{-1 / d_{\text{features}}}

    and the mutual-reachability distance within :math:`C` is
    :math:`d_{\text{mreach}}(x, y) = \max(a_{\text{coredist}}(x),
    a_{\text{coredist}}(y), d(x, y))`. A minimum spanning tree is built
    over each cluster's own mutual-reachability graph (reusing
    `tgmm.hdbscan.prim_mst`, the same Prim's-algorithm implementation
    `HDBSCAN` itself uses). **Density Sparseness of a Cluster** (DSC)
    is the maximum edge weight in that MST; **Density Separation
    between a Pair of Clusters** (DSPC) is the minimum
    mutual-reachability distance between an *internal* node (MST
    degree >= 2 -- excludes boundary/leaf points) of one cluster's MST
    and an internal node of the other's.

    .. note::
       For a tree with >= 3 nodes, every edge has at least one
       endpoint of degree >= 2 (an edge between two degree-1 nodes
       would disconnect the rest of the tree) -- so restricting DSC to
       "edges incident to an internal node" is equivalent to no
       restriction at all for any cluster with >= 3 points, which is
       why DSC below is simply the MST's maximum edge weight. The
       `internal`/leaf distinction is only load-bearing for DSPC,
       which compares nodes *across* two different clusters.

    .. math::
        V(C_i) = \frac{\min_j \text{DSPC}_{ij} - \text{DSC}_i}
                       {\max(\min_j \text{DSPC}_{ij}, \text{DSC}_i)},
        \qquad \text{DBCV} = \sum_i \frac{n_i}{n} V(C_i)

    with `n` counting noise points in the denominator (not the
    numerator) -- this *is* `dbcv`'s noise handling, which is why it
    does not go through `_apply_noise_scaling` the way the other
    internal indexes do.

    Clusters with fewer than 2 points contribute 0 (the all-points
    core distance needs at least one other point in the cluster to
    average over); a cluster whose MST has no internal nodes at all
    (every node is a leaf -- only possible for 2-point clusters) falls
    back to treating every node as internal for DSPC purposes, the
    standard practical fallback.

    Parameters
    ----------
    X : torch.Tensor
        Data, shape (n_samples, n_features).
    labels : torch.Tensor
        Cluster labels, shape (n_samples,). Need not be contiguous.
    metric : str, optional
        One of 'euclidean', 'manhattan', 'cosine', 'mahalanobis'
        (requires `VI`). (default: 'euclidean')
    noise_label : int, optional
        Label value marking noise points (HDBSCAN's convention is
        -1). Pass `None` if there is no noise label in `labels`.
        (default: -1)
    VI : torch.Tensor, optional
        `(d, d)` precision matrix for `metric='mahalanobis'`.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        DBCV score in `[-1, 1]` (higher is better).
    """
    labels = labels.to(torch.long)
    n = labels.shape[0]
    d_features = X.shape[1]

    if noise_label is not None:
        keep_mask = labels != noise_label
    else:
        keep_mask = torch.ones_like(labels, dtype=torch.bool)
    cluster_ids = torch.unique(labels[keep_mask], sorted=True).tolist()
    if len(cluster_ids) < 1:
        return 0.0

    per_cluster = {}
    for cid in cluster_ids:
        Xc = X[labels == cid]
        nc = Xc.shape[0]
        if nc < 2:
            per_cluster[cid] = dict(Xc=Xc, nc=nc, core_dist=None, internal_mask=None, dsc=0.0)
            continue

        D_full = ClusteringMetrics._pairwise_distances(Xc, Xc, metric, VI)
        D_safe = D_full.clone()
        D_safe.fill_diagonal_(float('inf'))
        D_safe = D_safe.clamp_min(1e-12)

        mean_inv_pow = D_safe.pow(-float(d_features)).sum(dim=1) / (nc - 1)
        core_dist = mean_inv_pow.pow(-1.0 / d_features)

        mreach = torch.maximum(torch.maximum(core_dist.unsqueeze(1), core_dist.unsqueeze(0)), D_full)
        mreach.fill_diagonal_(0.0)

        mst_edges = prim_mst(mreach)  # (nc - 1, 3): [u, v, weight], unsorted
        degree = torch.zeros(nc, dtype=torch.long)
        for u, v, _w in mst_edges:
            degree[int(u)] += 1
            degree[int(v)] += 1
        internal_mask = degree >= 2
        if not bool(internal_mask.any()):
            internal_mask = torch.ones(nc, dtype=torch.bool)

        dsc = float(mst_edges[:, 2].max())

        per_cluster[cid] = dict(Xc=Xc, nc=nc, core_dist=core_dist, internal_mask=internal_mask, dsc=dsc)

    total = 0.0
    for cid in cluster_ids:
        info_i = per_cluster[cid]
        if info_i['nc'] < 2:
            continue

        min_dspc = float('inf')
        Xi_int = info_i['Xc'][info_i['internal_mask']]
        core_i_int = info_i['core_dist'][info_i['internal_mask']]
        for other_id in cluster_ids:
            if other_id == cid:
                continue
            info_j = per_cluster[other_id]
            if info_j['nc'] < 2:
                continue
            Xj_int = info_j['Xc'][info_j['internal_mask']]
            core_j_int = info_j['core_dist'][info_j['internal_mask']]

            D_cross = ClusteringMetrics._pairwise_distances(Xi_int, Xj_int, metric, VI)
            mreach_cross = torch.maximum(
                torch.maximum(core_i_int.unsqueeze(1), core_j_int.unsqueeze(0)), D_cross
            )
            min_dspc = min(min_dspc, float(mreach_cross.min()))

        dsc_i = info_i['dsc']
        if min_dspc == float('inf'):
            v_i = 0.0  # no other non-trivial cluster to compare against
        else:
            denom = max(min_dspc, dsc_i)
            v_i = (min_dspc - dsc_i) / denom if denom > 0 else 0.0

        total += (info_i['nc'] / n) * v_i

    return total

$ \text{RI} = \frac{\text{TP} + \text{TN}}{\text{TP} + \text{TN} + \text{FP} + \text{FN}} $

Computed in float64 from the contingency table; labels need not be contiguous. Equal to sklearn.metrics.rand_score (RI is 1.0 when there are fewer than two samples).

@staticmethod
def rand_score(labels_true: torch.Tensor, labels_pred: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    r"""
    Rand Index (RI) measures the similarity between two clusterings.
    It counts the agreement of pairwise assignments.

    $ \text{RI} = \frac{\text{TP} + \text{TN}}{\text{TP} + \text{TN} + \text{FP} + \text{FN}} $

    Computed in float64 from the contingency table; labels need not be contiguous. Equal to
    `sklearn.metrics.rand_score` (RI is 1.0 when there are fewer than two samples).

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels_true : torch.Tensor
        Ground-truth labels, shape (n_samples,).
    labels_pred : torch.Tensor
        Predicted labels, shape (n_samples,).

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Rand Index in [0, 1].
    """
    n_samples = labels_true.size(0)
    contingency = ClusteringMetrics._contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred)
    n_pairs = n_samples * (n_samples - 1) / 2
    if n_pairs == 0:
        return 1.0
    sum_comb_c = (contingency.pow(2) - contingency).sum() / 2
    rows, cols = contingency.sum(dim=1), contingency.sum(dim=0)
    sum_comb = (rows.pow(2) - rows).sum() / 2
    sum_comb_pred = (cols.pow(2) - cols).sum() / 2

    tp = sum_comb_c
    fp = sum_comb_pred - tp
    fn = sum_comb - tp
    tn = n_pairs - tp - fp - fn
    return ((tp + tn) / (tp + fp + fn + tn)).item()

Computed in float64; labels need not be contiguous. Follows scikit-learn's special cases (ARI is 1.0 when both labelings are a single cluster, both put every sample alone, or there is nothing to compare).

@staticmethod
def adjusted_rand_score(labels_true: torch.Tensor, labels_pred: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    r"""
    Adjusted Rand Index (ARI), which adjusts RI for chance.

    $ \mathrm{ARI} = \frac{ \mathrm{RI} - \mathrm{E}[\mathrm{RI}] }{ \max(\mathrm{RI}) - \mathrm{E}[\mathrm{RI}] } $

    Computed in float64; labels need not be contiguous. Follows scikit-learn's special cases
    (ARI is 1.0 when both labelings are a single cluster, both put every sample alone, or there
    is nothing to compare).

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels_true : torch.Tensor
        Ground-truth labels.
    labels_pred : torch.Tensor
        Predicted labels.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        ARI in [-1, 1], though it’s typically in [0, 1].
    """
    n_samples = labels_true.size(0)
    contingency = ClusteringMetrics._contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred)
    n_classes, n_clusters = contingency.shape
    if n_classes == n_clusters == 1 or n_classes == n_clusters == 0 or n_classes == n_clusters == n_samples:
        return 1.0
    n_pairs = n_samples * (n_samples - 1) / 2
    sum_comb_c = (contingency.pow(2) - contingency).sum() / 2
    rows, cols = contingency.sum(dim=1), contingency.sum(dim=0)
    sum_comb = (rows.pow(2) - rows).sum() / 2
    sum_comb_pred = (cols.pow(2) - cols).sum() / 2

    expected_index = sum_comb * sum_comb_pred / n_pairs
    max_index = (sum_comb + sum_comb_pred) / 2
    denominator = max_index - expected_index
    if denominator == 0:
        return 1.0 if sum_comb_c == expected_index else 0.0
    return ((sum_comb_c - expected_index) / denominator).item()

Exact expected mutual information :math:E[\mathrm{MI}] of two random labelings with the given cluster sizes (the permutation / hypergeometric model; Vinh, Epps & Bailey, 2010, JMLR 11):

.. math:: E[\mathrm{MI}] = \sum_{i,j}\sum_{n_{ij}=\max(1,a_i+b_j-N)}^{\min(a_i,b_j)} \frac{n_{ij}}{N}\log\frac{N n_{ij}}{a_i b_j}\; \frac{a_i!\,b_j!\,(N-a_i)!\,(N-b_j)!}{N!\,n_{ij}!\,(a_i-n_{ij})!\,(b_j-n_{ij})!\,(N-a_i-b_j+n_{ij})!}

with row sums :math:a_i, column sums :math:b_j, :math:N samples. The summand depends on :math:(a_i, b_j) only, so equal cluster sizes are grouped and each distinct pair is evaluated once, vectorised over :math:n_{ij} with lgamma in float64. Adapted from scikit-learn's expected_mutual_information (BSD-3-Clause).

@staticmethod
def expected_mutual_information(contingency: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    r"""
    Exact expected mutual information :math:`E[\mathrm{MI}]` of two random labelings with the
    given cluster sizes (the permutation / hypergeometric model; Vinh, Epps & Bailey, 2010, JMLR 11):

    .. math::
        E[\mathrm{MI}] = \sum_{i,j}\sum_{n_{ij}=\max(1,a_i+b_j-N)}^{\min(a_i,b_j)}
          \frac{n_{ij}}{N}\log\frac{N n_{ij}}{a_i b_j}\;
          \frac{a_i!\,b_j!\,(N-a_i)!\,(N-b_j)!}{N!\,n_{ij}!\,(a_i-n_{ij})!\,(b_j-n_{ij})!\,(N-a_i-b_j+n_{ij})!}

    with row sums :math:`a_i`, column sums :math:`b_j`, :math:`N` samples. The summand depends on
    :math:`(a_i, b_j)` only, so equal cluster sizes are grouped and each distinct pair is evaluated
    once, vectorised over :math:`n_{ij}` with `lgamma` in float64. Adapted from scikit-learn's
    `expected_mutual_information` (BSD-3-Clause).
    """
    n = int(contingency.sum().item())
    rows = contingency.sum(dim=1).to(torch.long)
    cols = contingency.sum(dim=0).to(torch.long)
    ua, ca = torch.unique(rows, return_counts=True)
    ub, cb = torch.unique(cols, return_counts=True)
    dev = contingency.device
    f64 = torch.float64
    lg = torch.lgamma
    N = torch.tensor(float(n), dtype=f64, device=dev)
    total = torch.zeros((), dtype=f64, device=dev)
    ub_f = ub.to(f64)
    for a_val, a_cnt in zip(ua.tolist(), ca.tolist()):
        a = torch.tensor(float(a_val), dtype=f64, device=dev)
        lo = torch.clamp(a + ub_f - N, min=1.0)          # (B,) first n_ij
        hi = torch.clamp(ub_f, max=float(a_val))          # (B,) last n_ij
        width = int((hi - lo).max().item()) + 1
        if width <= 0:
            continue
        k = lo.unsqueeze(1) + torch.arange(width, dtype=f64, device=dev).unsqueeze(0)   # (B, W)
        valid = k <= hi.unsqueeze(1)
        k = torch.where(valid, k, lo.unsqueeze(1))        # keep every lgamma argument in range
        b = ub_f.unsqueeze(1)
        log_prob = (lg(a + 1) + lg(b + 1) + lg(N - a + 1) + lg(N - b + 1) - lg(N + 1)
                    - lg(k + 1) - lg(a - k + 1) - lg(b - k + 1) - lg(N - a - b + k + 1))
        term = (k / N) * (torch.log(N * k) - torch.log(a * b)) * torch.exp(log_prob)
        term = torch.where(valid, term, torch.zeros_like(term))
        total = total + a_cnt * (term.sum(dim=1) * cb.to(f64)).sum()
    return total.item()

@staticmethod
def adjusted_mutual_info_score(
    labels_true: torch.Tensor, labels_pred: torch.Tensor, average_method: str = 'arithmetic',
) -> float:
    r"""
    Adjusted Mutual Information (AMI; Vinh, Epps & Bailey, 2010):

    $$ \mathrm{AMI} = \frac{\mathrm{MI} - E[\mathrm{MI}]}{\operatorname{avg}(H(U), H(V)) - E[\mathrm{MI}]} $$

    with the **exact** expected mutual information (`expected_mutual_information`), so the value
    equals `sklearn.metrics.adjusted_mutual_info_score` for every `average_method`. Computed in
    float64; labels need not be contiguous.

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels_true : torch.Tensor
        Ground-truth labels.
    labels_pred : torch.Tensor
        Predicted labels.
    average_method : str, optional
        How to average the two entropies: 'arithmetic' (default), 'min', 'max' or 'geometric'.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        AMI (1 for identical partitions, about 0 for independent ones; can be slightly negative).
    """
    contingency = ClusteringMetrics._contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred)
    n_classes, n_clusters = contingency.shape
    if n_classes == n_clusters == 1 or n_classes == n_clusters == 0:
        return 1.0
    n = int(contingency.sum().item())
    mi = ClusteringMetrics._mutual_info_from_contingency(contingency)
    emi = ClusteringMetrics.expected_mutual_information(contingency)
    h_true = ClusteringMetrics._entropy_from_counts(contingency.sum(dim=1), n).item()
    h_pred = ClusteringMetrics._entropy_from_counts(contingency.sum(dim=0), n).item()
    normalizer = ClusteringMetrics._generalized_average(h_true, h_pred, average_method)
    denominator = normalizer - emi
    eps = torch.finfo(torch.float64).eps
    denominator = min(denominator, -eps) if denominator < 0 else max(denominator, eps)
    return (mi - emi) / denominator

@staticmethod
def fowlkes_mallows_score(labels_true: torch.Tensor, labels_pred: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    r"""
    Fowlkes-Mallows index (FM) = $ \sqrt{ \text{precision} \times \text{recall} } $.

    Computed in float64; 0.0 when no pair of samples is together in both labelings (as in
    scikit-learn) instead of `nan`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels_true : torch.Tensor
        Ground-truth labels.
    labels_pred : torch.Tensor
        Predicted labels.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        FM in [0, 1].
    """
    n_samples = labels_true.size(0)
    contingency = ClusteringMetrics._contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred)
    tp = contingency.pow(2).sum() - n_samples
    tp_fp = contingency.sum(dim=0).pow(2).sum() - n_samples
    tp_fn = contingency.sum(dim=1).pow(2).sum() - n_samples
    if tp == 0:
        return 0.0
    return (torch.sqrt(tp / tp_fp) * torch.sqrt(tp / tp_fn)).item()

    homogeneous regardless of partition).

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels_true : torch.Tensor
        Ground-truth labels, contiguous 0-indexed integers.
    labels_pred : torch.Tensor
        Predicted labels, contiguous 0-indexed integers.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Homogeneity in [0, 1].
    """
    n_samples = labels_true.size(0)
    contingency = ClusteringMetrics._contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred)
    class_counts = contingency.sum(dim=1)    # n_c
    cluster_counts = contingency.sum(dim=0)  # n_k

    h_c = ClusteringMetrics._entropy_from_counts(class_counts, n_samples)
    if h_c == 0:
        return 1.0

    p_joint = contingency / n_samples
    p_c_given_k = contingency / cluster_counts.clamp_min(1).unsqueeze(0)
    h_c_given_k = -torch.special.xlogy(p_joint, p_c_given_k).sum()

    return (1.0 - h_c_given_k / h_c).item()

@staticmethod
def completeness_score(labels_true: torch.Tensor, labels_pred: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    r"""
    Completeness: all members of a given class are assigned to the
    same cluster.

    $$ c = 1 - \frac{H(K \mid C)}{H(K)} $$

    (Rosenberg & Hirschberg, 2007), `H(K)` the entropy of the
    predicted cluster distribution, `H(K \mid C)` the entropy of the
    predicted cluster conditional on the true class. `c = 1.0` by
    convention when `H(K) = 0` (everything in one cluster, trivially
    complete regardless of the true classes).

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels_true : torch.Tensor
        Ground-truth labels, contiguous 0-indexed integers.
    labels_pred : torch.Tensor
        Predicted labels, contiguous 0-indexed integers.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Completeness in [0, 1].
    """
    n_samples = labels_true.size(0)
    contingency = ClusteringMetrics._contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred)
    class_counts = contingency.sum(dim=1)    # n_c
    cluster_counts = contingency.sum(dim=0)  # n_k

    h_k = ClusteringMetrics._entropy_from_counts(cluster_counts, n_samples)
    if h_k == 0:
        return 1.0

    p_joint = contingency / n_samples
    p_k_given_c = contingency / class_counts.clamp_min(1).unsqueeze(1)
    h_k_given_c = -torch.special.xlogy(p_joint, p_k_given_c).sum()

    return (1.0 - h_k_given_c / h_k).item()

@staticmethod
def v_measure_score(labels_true: torch.Tensor, labels_pred: torch.Tensor, beta: float = 1.0) -> float:
    r"""
    V-measure: the weighted harmonic mean of homogeneity and completeness.

    $$ V_\beta = \frac{(1 + \beta) \cdot h \cdot c}{\beta \cdot h + c} $$

    `beta=1.0` (default) weighs homogeneity and completeness equally
    and recovers the familiar `2hc / (h + c)` form; `beta > 1` weighs
    completeness more, `beta < 1` weighs homogeneity more.

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels_true : torch.Tensor
    labels_pred : torch.Tensor
    beta : float, optional
        Completeness/homogeneity weighting. (default: 1.0)

    Returns
    -------
    float
        V-measure in [0, 1].
    """
    h = ClusteringMetrics.homogeneity_score(labels_true, labels_pred)
    c = ClusteringMetrics.completeness_score(labels_true, labels_pred)
    denom = beta * h + c
    if denom == 0:
        return 0.0
    return (1.0 + beta) * h * c / denom

@staticmethod
def normalized_information_distance(labels_true: torch.Tensor, labels_pred: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    r"""
    Normalized Information Distance (Vinh, Epps & Bailey, 2010):

    $$ \text{NID} = 1 - \frac{I(U; V)}{\max(H(U), H(V))} $$

    a metric (satisfies the triangle inequality, unlike `1 - \text{NMI}`
    under some normalizations) in `[0, 1]`, `0` for identical
    partitions. Reuses `mutual_info_score` for `I(U; V)`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels_true : torch.Tensor
        Contiguous 0-indexed integers.
    labels_pred : torch.Tensor
        Contiguous 0-indexed integers.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        NID in [0, 1] (0 = identical partitions).
    """
    n_samples = labels_true.size(0)
    contingency = ClusteringMetrics._contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred)
    h_true = ClusteringMetrics._entropy_from_counts(contingency.sum(dim=1), n_samples)
    h_pred = ClusteringMetrics._entropy_from_counts(contingency.sum(dim=0), n_samples)
    max_h = torch.max(h_true, h_pred)

    if max_h == 0:
        return 0.0

    mi = ClusteringMetrics.mutual_info_score(labels_true, labels_pred)
    return (1.0 - mi / max_h.item())

@staticmethod
def purity_score(labels_true: torch.Tensor, labels_pred: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    r"""
    Purity score measures how many samples belong to the correct cluster.

    $ \mathrm{purity} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_k \max_j \lvert C_k \cap U_j \rvert $

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels_true : torch.Tensor
    labels_pred : torch.Tensor

    contingency = ClusteringMetrics._contingency_matrix(labels_true, labels_pred)

docs.text:
Compute a confusion matrix C with C[i, j] = number of samples whose true label is the i-th and whose predicted label is the j-th entry of labels.

By default labels is the sorted union of the true and predicted labels, so a predicted label that never occurs in labels_true gets its own (all-zero-row) entry instead of being silently dropped. If labels is given (as in scikit-learn) it fixes the order of rows and columns and samples whose true or predicted label is not in it are ignored.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default labels_true Tensor required labels_pred Tensor required labels sequence of int

Labels to index the matrix by, in order. (default: sorted union)

None

Returns:

Type Description Tensor

(C, C) int32 matrix, C the number of labels.

Source code in tgmm/metrics.py 
@staticmethod
def confusion_matrix(
    labels_true: torch.Tensor, labels_pred: torch.Tensor, labels: Optional[Sequence] = None,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    r"""
    Compute a confusion matrix `C` with `C[i, j]` = number of samples whose true label is the
    i-th and whose predicted label is the j-th entry of `labels`.

    By default `labels` is the sorted **union** of the true and predicted labels, so a predicted
    label that never occurs in `labels_true` gets its own (all-zero-row) entry instead of being
    silently dropped. If `labels` is given (as in scikit-learn) it fixes the order of rows and
    columns and samples whose true or predicted label is not in it are ignored.

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels_true : torch.Tensor
    labels_pred : torch.Tensor
    labels : sequence of int, optional
        Labels to index the matrix by, in order. (default: sorted union)

    Returns
    -------
    torch.Tensor
        `(C, C)` int32 matrix, `C` the number of labels.
    """
    device = labels_true.device
    lt = labels_true.to(torch.long).reshape(-1)
    lp = labels_pred.to(device=device, dtype=torch.long).reshape(-1)
    if labels is None:
        label_vals = torch.unique(torch.cat([lt, lp]))
    else:
        label_vals = torch.as_tensor(list(labels), dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    c = label_vals.numel()
    if c == 0:
        return torch.zeros((0, 0), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    order = torch.argsort(label_vals)
    sorted_vals = label_vals[order]

    def index_of(x):
        pos = torch.searchsorted(sorted_vals, x).clamp_(max=c - 1)
        ok = sorted_vals[pos] == x
        return order[pos], ok

    it, ok_t = index_of(lt)
    ip, ok_p = index_of(lp)
    keep = ok_t & ok_p
    cm = torch.zeros(c * c, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    cm.scatter_add_(0, (it * c + ip)[keep], torch.ones(int(keep.sum().item()), dtype=torch.int32, device=device))
    return cm.view(c, c)

Compute a simple classification report for each class: precision, recall, F1, Jaccard index, ROC-AUC, and support.

The classes are the sorted union of the true and predicted labels; a label that is only ever predicted has support 0, precision 0 and recall 0. The roc_auc entry is the one-vs-rest AUC of the hard predictions (roc_auc_score on 0/1 indicators), which for hard labels equals the balanced accuracy of that class; it is 1.0 by convention when the class is absent from labels_true.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default labels_true Tensor required labels_pred Tensor required

Returns:

Type Description dict

A dictionary keyed by class label, each containing: "precision", "recall", "f1-score", "support", "jaccard", "roc_auc".

Source code in tgmm/metrics.py 
@staticmethod
def classification_report(labels_true: torch.Tensor, labels_pred: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
    r"""
    Compute a simple classification report for each class: precision, recall, F1,
    Jaccard index, ROC-AUC, and support.

    The classes are the sorted union of the true and predicted labels; a label that is only ever
    predicted has `support` 0, precision 0 and recall 0. The `roc_auc` entry is the one-vs-rest AUC
    of the *hard* predictions (`roc_auc_score` on 0/1 indicators), which for hard labels equals
    the balanced accuracy of that class; it is 1.0 by convention when the class is absent from
    `labels_true`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels_true : torch.Tensor
    labels_pred : torch.Tensor

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A dictionary keyed by class label, each containing:
        "precision", "recall", "f1-score", "support", "jaccard", "roc_auc".
    """
    device = labels_true.device
    labels_pred = labels_pred.to(device)
    unique_labels = torch.unique(torch.cat([labels_true.reshape(-1), labels_pred.reshape(-1)]))
    report = {}

    for label in unique_labels:
        true_positives = ((labels_true == label) & (labels_pred == label)).sum().item()
        false_positives = ((labels_true != label) & (labels_pred == label)).sum().item()
        false_negatives = ((labels_true == label) & (labels_pred != label)).sum().item()

        precision = (true_positives / (true_positives + false_positives)
                     if (true_positives + false_positives) > 0 else 0.0)
        recall = (true_positives / (true_positives + false_negatives)
                  if (true_positives + false_negatives) > 0 else 0.0)
        f1_score = (2.0 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall)
                    if (precision + recall) > 0 else 0.0)
        support = (labels_true == label).sum().item()
        jaccard_index = (true_positives / (true_positives + false_positives + false_negatives)
                         if (true_positives + false_positives + false_negatives) > 0 else 0.0)

        binary_true = (labels_true == label).float().to(device)
        binary_pred = (labels_pred == label).float().to(device)
        roc_auc = ClusteringMetrics.roc_auc_score(binary_true, binary_pred)

        report[int(label)] = {
            "precision": precision,
            "recall": recall,
            "f1-score": f1_score,
            "support": support,
            "jaccard": jaccard_index,
            "roc_auc": roc_auc
        }

    return report

docs.text:
Binary ROC-AUC, computed as the Mann-Whitney U statistic with average ranks for ties:

\[ \mathrm{AUC} = \frac{\sum_{i:\,y_i=1} \operatorname{rank}(s_i) - n_+(n_+ + 1)/2}{n_+\, n_-} \]

so it is independent of the order of the samples, equals sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score, and for hard 0/1 predictions equals the balanced accuracy (the earlier trapezoid-over-argsort version depended on how ties happened to be sorted). If only one class is present it returns 1.0 by convention.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default labels_true Tensor

Binary ground-truth (0 or 1), shape (n_samples,).

required labels_pred Tensor

Binary predictions or real-valued scores/probabilities, shape (n_samples,).

required

Returns:

Type Description float

Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC).

Source code in tgmm/metrics.py 
@staticmethod
def roc_auc_score(labels_true: torch.Tensor, labels_pred: torch.Tensor) -> float:
    r"""
    Binary ROC-AUC, computed as the Mann-Whitney U statistic with **average ranks for ties**:

    $$ \mathrm{AUC} = \frac{\sum_{i:\,y_i=1} \operatorname{rank}(s_i) - n_+(n_+ + 1)/2}{n_+\, n_-} $$

    so it is independent of the order of the samples, equals `sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score`, and
    for hard 0/1 predictions equals the balanced accuracy (the earlier trapezoid-over-argsort
    version depended on how ties happened to be sorted). If only one class is present it returns
    1.0 by convention.

    Parameters
    ----------
    labels_true : torch.Tensor
        Binary ground-truth (0 or 1), shape (n_samples,).
    labels_pred : torch.Tensor
        Binary predictions or real-valued scores/probabilities, shape (n_samples,).

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC).
    """
    y = labels_true.reshape(-1).to(torch.float64) > 0
    n_pos = int(y.sum().item())
    n_neg = y.numel() - n_pos
    if n_pos == 0 or n_neg == 0:
        return 1.0  # degenerate: a single class (documented convention)

    scores = labels_pred.reshape(-1).to(device=y.device, dtype=torch.float64)
    _, inverse, counts = torch.unique(scores, return_inverse=True, return_counts=True)
    counts_f = counts.to(torch.float64)
    avg_rank = torch.cumsum(counts_f, dim=0) - (counts_f - 1.0) / 2.0   # 1-based average rank per tie group
    ranks = avg_rank[inverse]
    auc = (ranks[y].sum() - n_pos * (n_pos + 1) / 2.0) / (n_pos * n_neg)
    return auc.item()

@staticmethod
def kl_divergence_gmm(gmm_p, gmm_q, n_samples: int = 10000) -> float:
    r"""
    Approximate the KL divergence $D_{KL}(p \Vert q)$ between two
    Gaussian Mixture Models using Monte Carlo sampling from ``gmm_p``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    gmm_p : GaussianMixture
        The first GMM (interpreted as distribution p).
    gmm_q : GaussianMixture
        The second GMM (interpreted as distribution q).
    n_samples : int, optional
        Number of samples to draw from gmm_p for the Monte Carlo approximation
        (default: 10000).

    Returns
    -------
    float
        Approximated KL divergence $ \mathrm{E}_{x \sim p}[\log p(x) - \log q(x)]$.
    """
    device = gmm_p.device
    samples, _ = gmm_p.sample(n_samples)  # (n_samples, n_features)
    samples = samples.to(device)

    # Log-likelihood of samples under both GMMs
    log_p = gmm_p.score_samples(samples)
    log_q = gmm_q.score_samples(samples)

    kl_divergence = (log_p - log_q).mean().item()
    return kl_divergence

@staticmethod
def evaluate_clustering(
    gmm_model,
    X: torch.Tensor,
    true_labels: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
    metrics: Optional[list] = None
) -> dict:
    r"""
    Evaluate a fitted GMM using a set of requested metrics, possibly with ground-truth labels.

    Parameters
    ----------
    gmm_model : GaussianMixture
        A fitted GMM model (must have ``fitted_ == True``).
    X : torch.Tensor
        Data to evaluate, shape (n_samples, n_features).
    true_labels : torch.Tensor or None
        Ground-truth labels for supervised metrics (optional).
    metrics : list of str or None
        Which metrics to compute. If None, uses a default set.

    Returns
    -------
    results : dict
        A dictionary of metric_name -> metric_value pairs.

    Notes
    -----
    BIC/AIC are not computed here -- call ``gmm_model.bic(X)`` /
    ``gmm_model.aic(X)`` directly.
    """
    if not gmm_model.fitted_:
        raise ValueError("The GMM model must be fitted before evaluation.")

    if metrics is None:
        metrics = [
            # Supervised
            "rand_score", "adjusted_rand_score", "mutual_info_score",
            "normalized_mutual_info_score", "adjusted_mutual_info_score",
            "fowlkes_mallows_score", "homogeneity_score", "completeness_score",
            "v_measure_score", "purity_score",
            # Classification-based
            "classification_report", "confusion_matrix",
            # Unsupervised
            "silhouette_score", "davies_bouldin_index", "calinski_harabasz_score",
            "dunn_index",
        ]

    # Predict cluster labels
    pred_labels = gmm_model.predict(X).cpu()
    results = {}

    # If ground-truth labels provided, compute supervised metrics
    if true_labels is not None:
        true_labels = true_labels.cpu()

        if "rand_score" in metrics:
            results["rand_score"] = ClusteringMetrics.rand_score(true_labels, pred_labels)
        if "adjusted_rand_score" in metrics:
            results["adjusted_rand_score"] = ClusteringMetrics.adjusted_rand_score(true_labels, pred_labels)
        if "mutual_info_score" in metrics:
            results["mutual_info_score"] = ClusteringMetrics.mutual_info_score(true_labels, pred_labels)
        if "adjusted_mutual_info_score" in metrics:
            results["adjusted_mutual_info_score"] = ClusteringMetrics.adjusted_mutual_info_score(true_labels, pred_labels)
        if "normalized_mutual_info_score" in metrics:
            results["normalized_mutual_info_score"] = ClusteringMetrics.normalized_mutual_info_score(true_labels, pred_labels)
        if "fowlkes_mallows_score" in metrics:
            results["fowlkes_mallows_score"] = ClusteringMetrics.fowlkes_mallows_score(true_labels, pred_labels)
        if "homogeneity_score" in metrics:
            results["homogeneity_score"] = ClusteringMetrics.homogeneity_score(true_labels, pred_labels)
        if "completeness_score" in metrics:
            results["completeness_score"] = ClusteringMetrics.completeness_score(true_labels, pred_labels)
        if "v_measure_score" in metrics:
            results["v_measure_score"] = ClusteringMetrics.v_measure_score(true_labels, pred_labels)
        if "purity_score" in metrics:
            results["purity_score"] = ClusteringMetrics.purity_score(true_labels, pred_labels)
        if "classification_report" in metrics:
            results["classification_report"] = ClusteringMetrics.classification_report(true_labels, pred_labels)
        if "confusion_matrix" in metrics:
            results["confusion_matrix"] = ClusteringMetrics.confusion_matrix(true_labels, pred_labels)

    # Unsupervised metrics
    unique_pred_labels = torch.unique(pred_labels)
    if len(unique_pred_labels) > 1:
        if "silhouette_score" in metrics:
            results["silhouette_score"] = ClusteringMetrics.silhouette_score(
                X.cpu(), pred_labels, gmm_model.n_components
            )
        if "davies_bouldin_index" in metrics:
            results["davies_bouldin_index"] = ClusteringMetrics.davies_bouldin_index(
                X.cpu(), pred_labels, gmm_model.n_components
            )
        if "calinski_harabasz_score" in metrics:
            results["calinski_harabasz_score"] = ClusteringMetrics.calinski_harabasz_score(
                X.cpu(), pred_labels, gmm_model.n_components
            )
        if "dunn_index" in metrics:
            results["dunn_index"] = ClusteringMetrics.dunn_index(
                X.cpu(), pred_labels, gmm_model.n_components
            )

    return results

    n_components : int
    n_features : int
        ``d_m``, the number of unobserved coordinates.
    device, dtype
    """

    def __init__(self, weights, means, covariances, obs_dims, missing_dims):
        self.weights_ = weights
        self.means_ = means
        self.covariances_ = covariances
        self.obs_dims = list(obs_dims)
        self.missing_dims = list(missing_dims)
        self.n_components = weights.shape[1]
        self.n_features = means.shape[2]
        self.device = weights.device
        self.dtype = weights.dtype
        self._chol = None

    @property
    def n_samples(self) -> int:
        r"""Number of conditioning rows."""
        return self.weights_.shape[0]

    def _cholesky(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        if self._chol is None:
            self._chol = torch.linalg.cholesky(self.covariances_)
        return self._chol

    def mean(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        r"""
        Gaussian mixture regression: :math:`E[y\mid x_{o,i}]=\sum_kw_{ik}m_{ik}`.

        Returns
        -------
        torch.Tensor, shape (n, d_m)
        """
        return (self.weights_.unsqueeze(-1) * self.means_).sum(dim=1)

    def log_prob(self, Y: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        r"""
        :math:`\log p(y_i\mid x_{o,i})` for one query point per conditioning row.

        Parameters
        ----------
        Y : torch.Tensor, shape (n, d_m)
            Row ``i`` is evaluated under the mixture of row ``i``. A conditional
            with a single row (``n == 1``) is broadcast against any number of
            query points ``(m, d_m)``, which is how a single conditional
            density is evaluated on a grid.

        Returns
        -------
        torch.Tensor, shape (n,) (or (m,) in the single-row case)
        """
        Y = torch.as_tensor(Y, dtype=self.dtype, device=self.device)
        if Y.dim() != 2 or Y.shape[1] != self.n_features:
            raise ValueError(f"Y must have shape (n, {self.n_features}), got {tuple(Y.shape)}")
        if Y.shape[0] != self.n_samples and self.n_samples != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"Y has {Y.shape[0]} rows but the conditional has {self.n_samples}")
        L = self._cholesky()                                                    # (K, dm, dm)
        eye = torch.eye(self.n_features, dtype=self.dtype, device=self.device)
        L_inv = torch.linalg.solve_triangular(L, eye.expand_as(L), upper=False)  # (K, dm, dm)
        diff = Y.unsqueeze(1) - self.means_                                      # (n|m, K, dm)
        z = torch.einsum('kde,nke->nkd', L_inv, diff)
        maha = z.pow(2).sum(-1)                                                  # (n|m, K)
        log_det = 2.0 * torch.log(torch.diagonal(L, dim1=-2, dim2=-1)).sum(-1)   # (K,)
        log_n = -0.5 * (self.n_features * math.log(2.0 * math.pi) + log_det.unsqueeze(0) + maha)
        return torch.logsumexp(torch.log(self.weights_.clamp_min(1e-300)) + log_n, dim=1)

    def sample(self, n_draws: int = 1) -> torch.Tensor:
        r"""
        Draw from each row's conditional mixture.

        Parameters
        ----------
        n_draws : int, default=1
            Number of independent draws per conditioning row.

        Returns
        -------
        torch.Tensor, shape (n, n_draws, d_m)
        """
        if n_draws < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"n_draws must be >= 1, got {n_draws}")
        n = self.n_samples
        comp = torch.multinomial(self.weights_, n_draws, replacement=True)       # (n, n_draws)
        rows = torch.arange(n, device=self.device).unsqueeze(1).expand(n, n_draws)
        out = self.means_[rows, comp].clone()                                    # (n, n_draws, dm)
        eps = torch.randn(n, n_draws, self.n_features, dtype=self.dtype, device=self.device)
        L = self._cholesky()
        for k in range(self.n_components):                                       # loop over components, not samples
            sel = comp == k
            if sel.any():
                out[sel] += eps[sel] @ L[k].T
        return out

    def as_gmm(self, i: int):
        r"""
        The conditional distribution of row ``i`` as a fitted
        `GaussianMixture` over the missing coordinates (full covariance).
        """
        from ..gmm import GaussianMixture

        if not -self.n_samples <= i < self.n_samples:
            raise IndexError(f"row {i} out of range for {self.n_samples} conditioning rows")
        gmm = GaussianMixture(
            n_components=self.n_components, n_features=self.n_features, covariance_type='full',
            device=self.device,
        )
        gmm.dtype = self.dtype
        gmm.weights_ = self.weights_[i].clone()
        gmm.means_ = self.means_[i].clone()
        gmm.covariances_ = self.covariances_.clone()
        gmm.fitted_ = True
        gmm.converged_ = True
        gmm.n_components_ = self.n_components
        gmm.n_iter_ = 0
        gmm.lower_bound_ = float('nan')
        return gmm

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return (f"ConditionalGaussianMixture(n_samples={self.n_samples}, n_components={self.n_components}, "
                f"obs_dims={self.obs_dims}, missing_dims={self.missing_dims})")

def mstep_gpcm(
    code: str,
    W: torch.Tensor,
    nk: torch.Tensor,
    d: int,
    state: Optional[GPCMResult] = None,
    reg_covar: float = 0.0,
    gpcm_tol: float = 1e-6,
    gpcm_max_iter: int = 20,
) -> GPCMResult:
    r"""
    One M-step update for GPCM covariance code `code`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    code : str
        One of the 14 mclust codes (case-insensitive), see `GPCM_CODES`.
    W : torch.Tensor
        Per-component scatter, shape `(K, d, d)` -- `W_k = sum_i r_ik
        (x_i - ybar_k)(x_i - ybar_k)^T` (Phase 0's `stats.s2` for `full`
        covariance).
    nk : torch.Tensor
        Effective per-component sample counts, shape `(K,)`.
    d : int
        Number of features.
    state : GPCMResult, optional
        Previous M-step's result, used to warm-start the 5 iterative
        codes (`VEI`, `VEE`, `VEV`, `EVE`, `VVE`). Ignored by the other 9.
    reg_covar : float, optional
        Added to the assembled covariance's diagonal (not the
        decomposition). (default: 0.0)
    gpcm_tol : float, optional
        Relative-change stopping tolerance for the iterative codes'
        complete-data objective. (default: 1e-6)
    gpcm_max_iter : int, optional
        Maximum inner iterations for the iterative codes. (default: 20)

    Returns
    -------
    GPCMResult
    """
    code = code.upper()
    if code not in GPCM_CODES:
        raise ValueError(f"code must be one of {GPCM_CODES}, got {code!r}")

    K = W.shape[0]
    n = nk.sum()
    dtype, device = W.dtype, W.device
    I_d = torch.eye(d, dtype=dtype, device=device)

    diagW = torch.diagonal(W, dim1=-2, dim2=-1)  # (K, d) -- diag(W_k)

    # ===================================================================
    # Diagonal (axis-aligned, orientation = I) models: EII, VII, EEI, VVI
    # (the last 4 already have dedicated, tested code in tgmm/gmm.py --
    # implemented here too so tests can exercise all 14 codes uniformly).
    # ===================================================================
    if code == 'EII':
        lam = (diagW.sum()) / (n * d)
        volume, shape, orientation = lam, torch.ones(d, dtype=dtype, device=device), I_d
    elif code == 'VII':
        lam_k = diagW.sum(dim=-1) / (nk * d)
        volume, shape, orientation = lam_k, torch.ones(d, dtype=dtype, device=device), I_d
    elif code == 'EEI':
        b = diagW.sum(dim=0) / n  # (d,) -- this IS lambda * A already (free diagonal)
        volume, shape, orientation = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=dtype, device=device), b, I_d
    elif code == 'VVI':
        b_k = diagW / nk.unsqueeze(-1)  # (K, d)
        volume, shape, orientation = torch.ones(K, dtype=dtype, device=device), b_k, I_d

    # ===================================================================
    # VEI: volume varies, shape shared, axis-aligned. Iterative.
    # ===================================================================
    elif code == 'VEI':
        A = state.shape.clone() if (state is not None and state.shape.dim() == 1) else torch.ones(d, dtype=dtype, device=device)
        lam_k = None
        prev_J = None
        for _ in range(gpcm_max_iter):
            A_inv = 1.0 / A
            lam_k = (diagW * A_inv).sum(dim=-1) / (nk * d)
            B = (diagW / lam_k.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(dim=0)
            A = B / B.prod().clamp_min(1e-300).pow(1.0 / d)

            J = (nk * d * torch.log(lam_k)).sum() + (diagW * (1.0 / A) / lam_k.unsqueeze(-1)).sum()
            if prev_J is not None and abs(prev_J - J) < gpcm_tol * abs(prev_J).clamp_min(1e-300):
                break
            prev_J = J
        volume, shape, orientation = lam_k, A, I_d

    # ===================================================================
    # EVI: volume shared, shape varies, axis-aligned. Closed form.
    # ===================================================================
    elif code == 'EVI':
        B_k = diagW  # (K, d)
        det_B_k = B_k.prod(dim=-1).clamp_min(1e-300)  # (K,)
        A_k = B_k / det_B_k.unsqueeze(-1).pow(1.0 / d)
        lam = det_B_k.pow(1.0 / d).sum() / n
        volume, shape, orientation = lam, A_k, I_d

    # ===================================================================
    # EEV: volume & shape shared, orientation varies. Closed form.
    # ===================================================================
    elif code == 'EEV':
        eigvals, eigvecs = _eigh_descending(W)  # (K, d), (K, d, d)
        Omega = eigvals.sum(dim=0)  # (d,)
        det_Omega = Omega.prod().clamp_min(1e-300)
        A = Omega / det_Omega.pow(1.0 / d)
        lam = det_Omega.pow(1.0 / d) / n
        volume, shape, orientation = lam, A, eigvecs

    # ===================================================================
    # VEV: shape shared, volume & orientation vary. Iterative (D fixed
    # per-k from the data; lambda_k/A alternate).
    # ===================================================================
    elif code == 'VEV':
        eigvals, eigvecs = _eigh_descending(W)  # (K, d), (K, d, d) -- Omega_k, D_k
        A = state.shape.clone() if (state is not None and state.shape.dim() == 1) else torch.ones(d, dtype=dtype, device=device)
        lam_k = None
        prev_J = None
        for _ in range(gpcm_max_iter):
            A_inv = 1.0 / A
            lam_k = (eigvals * A_inv).sum(dim=-1) / (nk * d)
            Omega_sum = (eigvals / lam_k.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(dim=0)
            A = Omega_sum / Omega_sum.prod().clamp_min(1e-300).pow(1.0 / d)

            J = (nk * d * torch.log(lam_k)).sum() + (eigvals * (1.0 / A) / lam_k.unsqueeze(-1)).sum()
            if prev_J is not None and abs(prev_J - J) < gpcm_tol * abs(prev_J).clamp_min(1e-300):
                break
            prev_J = J
        volume, shape, orientation = lam_k, A, eigvecs

    # ===================================================================
    # EVV: volume shared, shape & orientation vary. Closed form.
    # ===================================================================
    elif code == 'EVV':
        det_W_k = torch.linalg.det(W).clamp_min(1e-300)  # (K,)
        C_k = W / det_W_k.view(K, 1, 1).pow(1.0 / d)
        lam = det_W_k.pow(1.0 / d).sum() / n
        eigvals, eigvecs = _eigh_descending(C_k)  # exposed shape_/orientation_ only
        volume, shape, orientation = lam, eigvals, eigvecs
        cov_full = lam * C_k + reg_covar * I_d.unsqueeze(0)
        return GPCMResult(volume=volume, shape=shape, orientation=orientation, cov_full=cov_full)

    # ===================================================================
    # VEE: shape & orientation shared (C = D A D^T, det 1), volume
    # varies. Iterative.
    # ===================================================================
    elif code == 'VEE':
        C = state.orientation.clone() @ torch.diag_embed(state.shape.clone()) @ state.orientation.clone().transpose(-1, -2) \
            if (state is not None and state.orientation.dim() == 2) else I_d.clone()
        lam_k = None
        prev_J = None
        for _ in range(gpcm_max_iter):
            C_inv = torch.linalg.inv(C)
            lam_k = torch.einsum('kij,ji->k', W, C_inv) / (nk * d)
            B = (W / lam_k.view(K, 1, 1)).sum(dim=0)
            det_B = torch.linalg.det(B).clamp_min(1e-300)
            C = B / det_B.pow(1.0 / d)

            C_inv = torch.linalg.inv(C)  # J is evaluated at the *updated* (lam_k, C)
            J = (nk * d * torch.log(lam_k)).sum() + torch.einsum('kij,ji->k', W, C_inv).div(lam_k).sum()
            if prev_J is not None and abs(prev_J - J) < gpcm_tol * abs(prev_J).clamp_min(1e-300):
                break
            prev_J = J
        eigvals, eigvecs = _eigh_descending(C)
        volume, shape, orientation = lam_k, eigvals, eigvecs
        cov_full = lam_k.view(K, 1, 1) * C.unsqueeze(0) + reg_covar * I_d.unsqueeze(0)
        return GPCMResult(volume=volume, shape=shape, orientation=orientation, cov_full=cov_full)

    # ===================================================================
    # EVE / VVE: orientation shared, shape varies, volume shared (EVE) or
    # varies (VVE). Iterative; the orientation sub-step is a Stiefel-
    # manifold optimization (no closed form).
    # ===================================================================
    elif code in ('EVE', 'VVE'):
        D = state.orientation.clone() if (state is not None and state.orientation.dim() == 2) else I_d.clone()
        A_k = None
        lam = None
        lam_k = None
        prev_J = None
        for _ in range(gpcm_max_iter):
            rotated = D.T @ W @ D  # (K, d, d)
            B_k = torch.diagonal(rotated, dim1=-2, dim2=-1)  # (K, d)
            det_B_k = B_k.prod(dim=-1).clamp_min(1e-300)
            A_k = B_k / det_B_k.unsqueeze(-1).pow(1.0 / d)
            A_k_inv = 1.0 / A_k

            if code == 'EVE':
                lam = (A_k_inv * B_k).sum() / (n * d)
                lam_vec = lam.expand(K)
            else:  # VVE
                lam_k = (A_k_inv * B_k).sum(dim=-1) / (nk * d)
                lam_vec = lam_k

            D = _optimize_orientation(W, A_k_inv, lam_vec, D)

            rotated = D.T @ W @ D
            B_k_check = torch.diagonal(rotated, dim1=-2, dim2=-1)
            J = (nk * d * torch.log(lam_vec)).sum() + (A_k_inv * B_k_check / lam_vec.unsqueeze(-1)).sum()
            if prev_J is not None and abs(prev_J - J) < gpcm_tol * abs(prev_J).clamp_min(1e-300):
                break
            prev_J = J

        volume = lam if code == 'EVE' else lam_k
        shape, orientation = A_k, D

    # ===================================================================
    # EEE, VVV: existing tgmm types ('tied_full', 'full'), implemented
    # here too only so every code is available through one interface for
    # testing -- tgmm/gmm.py keeps using its own dedicated code.
    # ===================================================================
    elif code == 'EEE':
        C = W.sum(dim=0) / n
        eigvals, eigvecs = _eigh_descending(C)
        volume, shape, orientation = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=dtype, device=device), eigvals, eigvecs
        cov_full = C.unsqueeze(0).expand(K, d, d).clone() + reg_covar * I_d.unsqueeze(0)
        return GPCMResult(volume=volume, shape=shape, orientation=orientation, cov_full=cov_full)
    elif code == 'VVV':
        C_k = W / nk.view(K, 1, 1)
        eigvals, eigvecs = _eigh_descending(C_k)
        volume, shape, orientation = torch.ones(K, dtype=dtype, device=device), eigvals, eigvecs
        cov_full = C_k + reg_covar * I_d.unsqueeze(0)
        return GPCMResult(volume=volume, shape=shape, orientation=orientation, cov_full=cov_full)
    else:  # pragma: no cover -- exhaustive above
        raise AssertionError(code)

    cov_full = _assemble_full(volume, shape, orientation, K, d, reg_covar)
    return GPCMResult(volume=volume, shape=shape, orientation=orientation, cov_full=cov_full)

class GPCMResult:
    r"""
    The decomposition :math:`\Sigma_k = \lambda_k D_k A_k D_k^T` an
    `mstep_gpcm` call produced.

    Attributes
    ----------
    volume : torch.Tensor
        Scalar (E-volume models) or shape `(K,)` (V-volume models).
    shape : torch.Tensor
        Shape `(d,)` (E-shape models) or `(K, d)` (V-shape models).
        Diagonal of `A_k`, determinant 1 for the 8 codes `GaussianMixture`
        actually uses this for (`VEI`, `EVI`, `VEE`, `EVE`, `EEV`, `VVE`,
        `VEV`, `EVV`). The 6 classic codes (`EII`, `VII`, `EEI`, `VVI`,
        `EEE`, `VVV`) are also available through `mstep_gpcm`, but there
        `volume` is 1 and `shape` holds the unnormalized variances /
        eigenvalues (the decomposition is trivially absorbed into `shape`).
    orientation : torch.Tensor
        Shape `(d, d)` (E- or I-orientation models) or `(K, d, d)`
        (V-orientation models).
    cov_full : torch.Tensor
        Assembled `(K, d, d)` covariance matrices, `reg_covar * I` already
        added.
    """

    volume: torch.Tensor
    shape: torch.Tensor
    orientation: torch.Tensor
    cov_full: torch.Tensor

Bases: BaseMixture

A Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) based on Expectation-Maximisation (EM) implemented in PyTorch.

This GMM supports: - The Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm - The Classification EM (CEM) algorithm as an alternative to standard EM - Multiple random initializations (n_init) - Configurable covariance types (full, diag, spherical, tied_full, tied_diag, tied_spherical) - Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) and Maximum a Posteriori (MAP) estimation with priors - Bayesian/Akaike information criteria (bic, aic) for model selection

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n_components int or None

Number of mixture components. If None, selects Gibbs-sampling mode: the number of components is inferred during fit (up to max_components) instead of fixed in advance, and mean_prior, mean_precision_prior, covariance_prior, and degrees_of_freedom_prior become required. See max_components, alpha, and suggest_priors. (default: None)

None n_features int

Dimensionality of the input data (number of features). If None, inferred from data. (default: None)

None covariance_type str

Type of covariance parameters to use. Either a tgmm name -- 'full', 'diag', 'spherical', 'tied_full', 'tied_diag', 'tied_spherical' -- or any of the 14 Celeux & Govaert (1995) GPCM mclust codes (case-insensitive): 'EII', 'VII', 'EEI', 'VEI', 'EVI', 'VVI', 'EEE', 'VEE', 'EVE', 'EEV', 'VVE', 'VEV', 'EVV', 'VVV' (the six tgmm names are aliases for 'EII'/'VII'/'EEI'/'VVI'/'EEE'/'VVV' respectively -- see covariance_type_, and the "GPCM Covariance Models" user-guide page for the 8 codes without a tgmm name). Aliases: 'tied' → 'tied_full', 'isotropic' → 'spherical'. (default: 'full')

'full' max_iter int

EM mode: maximum number of EM iterations to perform; EM stops early once the relative log-likelihood improvement drops below tol (see tol). Gibbs mode (n_components=None): the exact number of Gibbs sweeps run -- there is no early-stopping / convergence check in Gibbs mode (see converged_), so fit() always runs precisely max_iter sweeps, never fewer. Each Gibbs sweep is an O(n_samples) Python-level loop over every point (measured ~0.114 ms/point/sweep), so the shared default of 1000 can mean tens of minutes at moderate n_samples (e.g. roughly 19 minutes at n_samples=10,000). The default is left unchanged here so existing EM-tuned code isn't surprised by a different value -- when using Gibbs mode, pass an explicit, usually much smaller, max_iter instead of relying on this default. (default: 1000)

1000 tol float

Convergence threshold based on relative improvement in log-likelihood. (default: 1e-4)

0.0001 reg_covar float

Non-negative regularization added to the diagonal of covariance matrices to prevent singularity. (default: 1e-6)

1e-06 n_init int

Number of random initializations to try. The best run (highest log-likelihood) is kept. When n_init > 1, each initialization uses random_state + i as its seed to ensure both reproducibility and diversity. (default: 1)

1 init_means str or Tensor

Method for initializing means, or a tensor of initial means. - If str: 'kmeans', 'kpp', 'random', 'points', 'maxdist' - If tensor: shape (n_components, n_features) exactly (no broadcasting) (default: 'kmeans')

'kmeans' init_weights str or Tensor

Method for initializing weights, or a tensor of initial weights. - If str: 'uniform', 'random', 'kmeans' - If tensor: shape (n_components,) (default: 'uniform')

'uniform' init_covariances str or Tensor

Method for initializing covariances, or a tensor of initial covariances. - If str: 'empirical', 'eye', 'random', 'global' - If tensor: shape depends on covariance_type (supports broadcasting) * full: (n_features, n_features) or (n_components, n_features, n_features) * diag: (n_features,) or (n_components, n_features) * spherical: scalar or (n_components,) (default: 'empirical')

'empirical' random_state int or None

Random seed for reproducibility. If None, uses PyTorch's internal seed. When n_init > 1, serves as the base seed (initialization i uses random_state + i). (default: None)

None warm_start bool

If True, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit as initialization. (default: False)

False algorithm str

Which EM variant to run: 'em' (standard); 'cem' (Classification EM, hard assignment between the E- and M-steps); 'sem' (Stochastic EM, Celeux & Diebolt 1985 -- samples a hard assignment from the responsibilities each iteration instead of taking the argmax; use it to escape poor local optima or to detect an overspecified K via n_empty_components_); or 'saem' (Stochastic Approximation EM, Delyon, Lavielle & Moulines 1999 -- SEM with a step_size-weighted running-statistics blend across iterations, which does converge pointwise, unlike plain SEM). Gibbs mode (n_components=None) only supports 'em'. (default: 'em')

'em' cem bool

Deprecated; use algorithm='cem' instead. If True, raises a DeprecationWarning and is treated as algorithm='cem'. Passing cem=True together with an explicit algorithm other than 'em' or 'cem' raises ValueError. (default: False)

False batch_size int or None

If set, the E-step and sufficient-statistics accumulation process X in row chunks of this size instead of all at once, bounding peak memory to roughly O(batch_size * n_components * n_features) regardless of n_samples. With step_size=None (the default) this is purely a memory/speed trade-off: results are the same (up to ordinary floating-point summation-order differences) as batch_size=None. With step_size set, batch_size instead becomes the mini-batch size for online EM -- see step_size. (default: None)

None convergence str

Stopping rule used by the EM/CEM/SAEM loop (SEM never checks convergence; see algorithm): 'relative' (stop when the relative change in mean log-likelihood drops below tol, as before) or 'aitken' (stop once the Aitken-accelerated estimate of the asymptotic log-likelihood is within tol of the current value, which can detect convergence earlier on slowly-crawling fits; falls back to the relative rule for any iteration where the Aitken acceleration factor is undefined or >= 1). (default: 'relative')

'relative' temperature tuple of (float, int) or None

Deterministic annealing EM (Ueda & Nakano, 1998), for algorithm in ('em', 'cem', 'sem'). (beta_0, n_anneal): the E-step's joint log-density is scaled by a temperature beta that increases geometrically from beta_0 (in (0, 1)) at iteration 0 to 1.0 at iteration n_anneal and is held at 1.0 after. Convergence checks are suspended while beta < 1.0. Use this when initialization is unreliable (e.g. a saddle point equidistant from several true clusters) -- annealing smooths the likelihood surface early on, when standard EM would otherwise get stuck. The schedule actually used is recorded in annealing_schedule_. None disables annealing (beta fixed at 1.0, today's behaviour). (default: None)

None step_size float, str, or callable

Enables online/mini-batch EM for algorithm='em' (requires batch_size to also be set) and controls algorithm='saem''s stochastic-approximation step size (Cappé & Moulines, 2009; Delyon, Lavielle & Moulines, 1999). A float is a constant step size; 'auto' resolves to gamma_t = (t + 2) ** -0.7 (the documented default, t the running update count -- mini-batches for 'em', iterations for 'saem'); a callable t -> gamma_t gives a custom schedule. For algorithm='saem', None (the default) is treated as 'auto' rather than raising, since SAEM's convergence depends on a decaying step size by construction. For algorithm='em', None (the default) keeps batch_size as a pure memory optimization (exact EM) rather than switching to online EM. (default: None)

None sem_burn_in int or None

algorithm='sem' only: sweeps excluded from the sem_estimate selection below. If None, resolved to max_iter // 5. (default: None)

None sem_estimate str

algorithm='sem' only: how to summarise the post-burn-in sweeps into a final estimate. 'best' keeps the sweep with the highest observed log-likelihood; 'mean' averages weights_/means_/ covariances_ across every post-burn-in sweep (the covariance average is a plain arithmetic mean, which stays positive semi-definite). Averaging assumes no label switching across sweeps -- when K may be overspecified, prefer 'best'. (default: 'best')

'best' weight_concentration_prior Tensor or None

Dirichlet concentration prior for the mixture weights (MAP estimation). Shape: (n_components,) or scalar to broadcast. (default: None)

None mean_prior Tensor or None

Prior for the component means (MAP estimation). Must be used with mean_precision_prior. Shape: (n_features,) or (n_components, n_features). (default: None)

None mean_precision_prior float or None

Precision (inverse variance) of the mean prior (MAP estimation). (default: None)

None covariance_prior Tensor or None

Prior for the covariances (MAP estimation). Must be used with degrees_of_freedom_prior. Shape depends on covariance_type (supports broadcasting like init_covariances). (default: None)

None degrees_of_freedom_prior float or None

Degrees of freedom for the Wishart/Inverse-Wishart prior on covariances (MAP). Must be > n_features - 1. (default: None)

None max_components int or None

Gibbs mode only (n_components=None): upper bound on the number of components tracked during sampling. Ignored in EM mode. (default: 20)

20 alpha float

Gibbs mode only: Dirichlet process concentration parameter, controlling how readily new components are proposed. Ignored in EM mode. (default: 1.0)

1.0 burn_in int or None

Gibbs mode, unbounded variant only (max_components=None): number of initial sweeps excluded when recording n_components_history_ (the per-sweep active-component-count trace). Does not affect the fitted weights_/means_/ covariances_ themselves -- those are always taken from the final sweep regardless of burn_in, in both truncated and unbounded Gibbs mode. Ignored entirely in truncated Gibbs mode (max_components is an int) and in EM mode. If None, resolved internally to max(1, max_iter // 5). (default: None)

None weight_threshold float or None

Gibbs mode only: a component is treated as inactive (excluded from active_/n_components_) when its expected point count -- weight_i * n_samples, not the raw weight/probability itself -- is not greater than this threshold. E.g. the resolved default of 1.0 means "expected to own at most one point." Ignored in EM mode. (default: None, resolved internally to 1.0)

None init_k int or None

Gibbs mode only: number of components to seed the sampler with. Ignored in EM mode. (default: None)

None noise bool

Add a uniform noise component (Banfield & Raftery, 1993): a parameter-free extra mixture component with density 1 / V. Responsibilities then have shape (n_samples, n_components + 1) (last column = noise), predict returns -1 for points the noise component explains best, and weights_ holds the component weights, which sum to 1 - noise_weight_. Not supported with Gibbs mode, labels=, online EM / partial_fit, weight_concentration_prior or constrained sample. (default: False)

False noise_volume bbox or float

Volume V of the noise region: the bounding box of the fit data, or a user-supplied hypervolume. Ignored by VonMisesFisherMixture (uniform on the sphere). (default: 'bbox')

'bbox' noise_prior float

Initial noise weight pi_0, in (0, 1). (default: 0.05)

0.05 noise_init array - like

Per-sample initial noise indicator: a bool mask (True = noise) or cluster labels with -1 = noise (e.g. HDBSCAN(...).labels_). Overrides noise_prior; the initial parameters are computed from the unflagged rows. (default: None)

None frozen_components sequence of int

Indices of components whose means_ / covariances_ are held at their initial values for the whole fit (set them with tensor init_means / init_covariances, or warm_start); their mixing weights still update, and priors never shrink them. Not available for the tied covariance types or the 8 GPCM codes without a classic name (a factor is shared across components) and not in Gibbs mode. (default: ())

() missing (error, em)

How NaN entries of X are handled. 'error' (default): NaN raises ValueError. 'em': NaN marks missing-at-random values and the likelihood of the observed entries is maximised by EM (rows are grouped by missingness pattern; the E-step uses the marginal N(x_o; mu_o, Sigma_oo) and the M-step statistics use the conditional mean/covariance of the missing block). Works for every covariance type, algorithm in {'em', 'cem', 'sem', 'saem'}, temperature and batch_size; predict, predict_proba, score_samples, score, bic/aic/icl accept incomplete rows and impute(X) fills them in. Not supported with noise=True, Gibbs mode, labels=, online EM / partial_fit. On data without NaN the result is identical to 'error'. (default: 'error')

'error' verbose bool

If True, print progress during EM iterations. (default: False)

False verbose_interval int

Frequency (in iterations) at which to print progress when verbose=True. (default: 10)

10 device str or None

Device on which to run computations ('cpu' or 'cuda'). If None, uses GPU if available, otherwise CPU. (default: None)

None

Attributes:

Name Type Description weights_ Tensor

Mixture component weights of shape (n_components,).

means_ Tensor

Mixture component means of shape (n_components, n_features).

covariances_ Tensor

Mixture component covariances. Shape depends on covariance_type.

initial_weights_ Tensor

Initial mixture component weights before EM optimization, shape (n_components,).

initial_means_ Tensor

Initial mixture component means before EM optimization, shape (n_components, n_features).

initial_covariances_ Tensor

Initial mixture component covariances before EM optimization.

dtype dtype

Floating point dtype used for all model parameters. Set to the dtype of the data passed to fit (e.g. torch.float64 is fully supported), or torch.get_default_dtype() before the first call to fit.

fitted_ bool

Whether the model has been fitted.

converged_ bool

Whether the EM algorithm converged in the best run. In Gibbs mode (n_components=None), this is unconditionally True after fit() regardless of how many sweeps ran or any actual convergence assessment -- Gibbs sampling has no equivalent of EM's log-likelihood-plateau stopping criterion, so this flag does not indicate sampler convergence there (and sample()'s "did not converge" warning, gated on this flag, can never fire for a Gibbs-mode fit). If precision matters for a Gibbs-mode fit, inspect n_components_history_ (unbounded mode only) for component-count stability across sweeps, or increase max_iter.

n_iter_ int

Number of EM iterations performed in the best run.

lower_bound_ float

Log-likelihood lower bound on the fitted data for the best run.

best_random_state_ int or None

The random state that produced the best result when n_init > 1. Useful for reproducing the specific best initialization.

n_components_ int or None

Number of components after fitting. Equal to n_components in EM mode; in Gibbs mode, the inferred count (set once fit() supports Gibbs mode). None before the first fit.

active_ Tensor or None

Gibbs mode only: boolean/index mask of which of the tracked max_components slots are active in the fitted result. None in EM mode and before the first fit.

classes_ Tensor or None

Sorted distinct non--1 label values seen by the most recent fit(X, labels=...) call (supervised or semi-supervised); class_of_component_[k] indexes into classes_ for component k's class. None after an unsupervised fit (no labels) or before the first fit. Not persisted by save/load or save_state_dict/load_state_dict.

class_of_component_ Tensor or None

Shape (n_components,): which class (an index into classes_) each component belongs to, per components_per_class. None after an unsupervised fit or before the first fit.

log_likelihood_history_ Tensor or None

Per-iteration/sweep/epoch mean log-likelihood trace from the most recent EM-mode fit (every algorithm, including online EM). None before the first fit, and in Gibbs mode (which has no equivalent notion of a monotone trace to record).

annealing_schedule_ list of float or None

The beta value actually used at each E-step of the most recent fit, when temperature is set. None otherwise.

n_empty_components_ int

algorithm='sem' only: total number of component re-seeds across every sweep of the most recent fit (a component emptying out is evidence n_components may be too large for the data). 0 for every other algorithm.

covariance_type_ str

The canonical mclust GPCM code for covariance_type (e.g. 'VVV' for covariance_type='full'), always set regardless of which name/code was passed to the constructor.

volume_ Tensor or None

GPCM decomposition Sigma_k = volume_k * orientation_k @ diag(shape_k) @ orientation_k^T: scalar (E-volume models) or shape (n_components,) (V-volume models). Set after the first fit for the 8 new GPCM covariance types ('VEI', 'EVI', 'VEE', 'EVE', 'EEV', 'VVE', 'VEV', 'EVV'); None for the 6 pre-existing types.

shape_ Tensor or None

See volume_: shape (n_features,) (E-shape models) or (n_components, n_features) (V-shape models), determinant 1.

orientation_ Tensor or None

See volume_: shape (n_features, n_features) (E- or I-orientation models) or (n_components, n_features, n_features) (V-orientation models).

class GaussianMixture(BaseMixture):
    r"""
    A Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) based on Expectation-Maximisation (EM) implemented in PyTorch.

    This GMM supports:
    - The Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm
    - The Classification EM (CEM) algorithm as an alternative to standard EM
    - Multiple random initializations (n_init)
    - Configurable covariance types (full, diag, spherical, tied_full, tied_diag, tied_spherical)
    - Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) and Maximum a Posteriori (MAP) estimation with priors
    - Bayesian/Akaike information criteria (`bic`, `aic`) for model selection

    Parameters
    ----------
    n_components : int or None, optional
        Number of mixture components. If None, selects Gibbs-sampling mode:
        the number of components is inferred during `fit` (up to
        `max_components`) instead of fixed in advance, and mean_prior,
        mean_precision_prior, covariance_prior, and degrees_of_freedom_prior
        become required. See `max_components`, `alpha`, and `suggest_priors`.
        (default: None)
    n_features : int, optional
        Dimensionality of the input data (number of features). If None, inferred from data. (default: None)
    covariance_type : str, optional
        Type of covariance parameters to use. Either a tgmm name --
        'full', 'diag', 'spherical', 'tied_full', 'tied_diag',
        'tied_spherical' -- or any of the 14 Celeux & Govaert (1995) GPCM
        mclust codes (case-insensitive): 'EII', 'VII', 'EEI', 'VEI', 'EVI',
        'VVI', 'EEE', 'VEE', 'EVE', 'EEV', 'VVE', 'VEV', 'EVV', 'VVV' (the
        six tgmm names are aliases for 'EII'/'VII'/'EEI'/'VVI'/'EEE'/'VVV'
        respectively -- see `covariance_type_`, and the "GPCM Covariance
        Models" user-guide page for the 8 codes without a tgmm name).
        Aliases: 'tied' → 'tied_full', 'isotropic' → 'spherical'.
        (default: 'full')
    max_iter : int, optional
        EM mode: maximum number of EM iterations to perform; EM stops
        early once the relative log-likelihood improvement drops below
        `tol` (see `tol`). Gibbs mode (`n_components=None`): the *exact*
        number of Gibbs sweeps run -- there is no early-stopping /
        convergence check in Gibbs mode (see `converged_`), so `fit()`
        always runs precisely `max_iter` sweeps, never fewer. Each Gibbs
        sweep is an O(n_samples) Python-level loop over every point
        (measured ~0.114 ms/point/sweep), so the shared default of 1000
        can mean tens of minutes at moderate `n_samples` (e.g. roughly
        19 minutes at n_samples=10,000). The default is left unchanged
        here so existing EM-tuned code isn't surprised by a different
        value -- when using Gibbs mode, pass an explicit, usually much
        smaller, `max_iter` instead of relying on this default.
        (default: 1000)
